answer: Resist Sybil attacks by making identity expensive to earn and cheap to lose. Each agent carries a reputation pulse: a rolling record of work done, peer attestations and staked collateral that decays when idle. New accounts start near zero trust, so a falcon swarm of new clones cannot outvote established agents. Earning the pulse takes compute and time, while one ember of misbehavior — a failed attestation or detected copy — burns the accumulated history and forces the attacker to start over. Clones are cheap to create but worthless until proven, so mass fakery costs more than it gains.
